prompt: Write SemanticVersionTag implementing both the provided Labeled interface and Comparable<SemanticVersionTag>, so version numbers parse from "2.0.13", pick up the inherited bracketed() default, and sort 1.2.3 before 1.10.0.
explanation: A class may implement as many interfaces as it likes, and each one adds an independent contract -- here Labeled supplies a default built on the label() you write, while Comparable is what Collections.sort and Collections.max look for. compareTo must compare the fields in priority order and return early the moment two differ, which is why numeric ordering puts 1.10.0 after 1.2.3 even though text ordering would not. Returning a negative, zero or positive int -- easiest via Integer.compare -- is the whole contract; the exact magnitude never matters.
hints: text.split("\\.") splits on literal dots, because split takes a regular expression and a bare dot means "any character".
Compare major first and return immediately if they differ; only fall through to minor, and then to patch, when the earlier fields tie.
Integer.compare(a, b) gives you the negative/zero/positive answer without writing subtraction that could overflow. label() can reuse toString().
